did_you_know.text: The name Paddan-Aram is usually understood as “the plain of Aram.” It refers to a region in northern Mesopotamia, around Harran.
The word “Aramean” describes Laban’s origin in the region of Aram, not a nationality in the sense of modern countries.
The Hebrew verb vayifga can mean reaching or coming upon a place, not necessarily meeting a person by chance.
The word sullam appears only here in the Bible, so its exact meaning is uncertain; tradition knows it as “Jacob’s ladder.”
The phrase “westward, eastward, northward, and southward” describes the four directions. In Biblical Hebrew, yamah means westward, toward the sea.
A matzevah was a standing stone that could serve as a memorial or sacred marker in the ancient world. Pouring oil on it expressed dedication.
The Hebrew word ma’aser means a tenth, or one part out of ten. In his vow, Jacob connects receiving blessing with giving in return.
